'''Peter J. H. Scott''' [[Fellow of the Royal Society of Chemistry|FRSC]] [[Chartered Chemist|CChem]] (born July 27, 1979) is a British and American chemist and radiochemist who is the Paul L. Carson Collegiate Professor of Radiology at the [[University of Michigan]] in the United States. He is also a professor of radiology, professor of pharmacology and professor of medicinal chemistry, and a core member of the [[University_of_Michigan_Rogel_Cancer_Center|Rogel Cancer Center]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://medicine.umich.edu/dept/radiology|title=Radiology {{!}} Michigan Medicine {{!}} University of Michigan|website=medicine.umich.edu|date=January 6, 2014|access-date=May 1, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://pharmacy.umich.edu/medchem|title=Medicinal Chemistry {{!}} UM College of Pharmacy|website=pharmacy.umich.edu|access-date=May 1, 2019}}</ref>  He is Chief of Nuclear Medicine and director of the University of Michigan Positron Emission Tomography ([[Positron emission tomography|PET]]) Center,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://medicine.umich.edu/dept/radiology/research/pet-center|title=PET Center {{!}} Radiology {{!}} Michigan Medicine {{!}} University of Michigan|website=medicine.umich.edu|date=January 30, 2014|access-date=May 1, 2019}}</ref> and runs a research group developing new [[radiochemistry]] methodology and novel PET [[Radioactive tracer|radiotracers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mcommunity.umich.edu/#profile:pjhscott|title=Peter J. Scott profile|website=mcommunity.umich.edu}}</ref>

== Life ==
Peter Scott was born and grew up in North East England and attended [[Whitley Bay High School]]. He received his undergraduate degree with [[British undergraduate degree classification#First-class honours|first class honors]] in medicinal and pharmaceutical chemistry from [[Loughborough University]] in 2001, after conducting research with Raymond Jones. He subsequently obtained his PhD in organic chemistry from [[Durham University]] in 2005, where he was a member of [[Ustinov College]], under the mentorship of Patrick G. Steel. Scott then moved to the United States to undertake postdoctoral research in organometallic chemistry at [[University at Buffalo|SUNY Buffalo]] under [[Huw Davies (chemist)|Huw Davies]], and PET radiochemistry at the University of Michigan with Michael Kilbourn.

== Research ==
Scott runs a research group developing new metal-catalyzed methods for incorporating [[fluorine-18]] and [[Isotopes of carbon#Carbon-11|carbon-11]] into bioactive molecules as well as novel PET [[Radioactive tracer|radiotracers]] for imaging [[Neurodegeneration|neurodegenerative disorders]]. His methodology work aims to improve the synthesis of PET radiotracers and he has an active collaboration with [[Melanie Sanford|Prof. Melanie Sanford's]] group<ref>{{cite web|title=UM scientists improve synthesis of PET imaging molecules|last=Haynes|first=Sarah|date=October 3, 2018|website=lsa.umich.edu|url=https://lsa.umich.edu/chem/news-events/all-news/search-news/um-scientists-improve-synthesis-of-pet-imaging-molecules.html}}</ref> that is funded by [[National_Institute_of_Biomedical_Imaging_and_Bioengineering|NIBIB]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://grantome.com/grant/NIH/R01-EB021155-04|title = Copper-mediated Late-Stage Radiofluorination of Electron-rich Arenes|last1 = Scott|first1 = Peter|last2 = Sanford|first2 = Melanie}}</ref> Together they have developed methods for the Cu-mediated [[radiofluorination]]<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Wright|first1=Jay S.|last2=Kaur|first2=Tanpreet|last3=Preshlock|first3=Sean|last4=Tanzey|first4=Sean S.|last5=Winton|first5=Wade P.|last6=Sharninghausen|first6=Liam S.|last7=Wiesner|first7=Nicholas|last8=Brooks|first8=Allen F.|last9=Sanford|first9=Melanie S.|last10=Scott|first10=Peter J.
